description:
Query SEC filings by form type, date range, CIK and/or 8-K item.

Returns deduplicated filing metadata sorted by filing date (newest first). Each
filing's content_object lists its documents (filename, doc_type, description,
sequence; sequence 1 is the primary document); read any of them with
get_document(cik, accession_number, filename). A document's link, to cite, is
beatandraise_base_url + filename (the beatandraise.com viewer); the filing's own
source gives the primary document's link and a ready-made citation. Each filing
also carries its items (an 8-K's, e.g. "2.02 Results of Operations and Financial
Condition") when it has any. The R*.htm files are XBRL financial-table
pages; list_filing_tables says which table each one is.

An 8-K carries a headline when its press release (EX-99.1) has one, e.g.
"Tesla Third Quarter 2026 Production, Deliveries & Deployments": read from the
release's opening lines by rules, so use it to choose which 8-K to read, not as
a quotation (about 2% are another line of the release; verify_quote before
quoting). No headline says nothing about the filing: its exhibit may be a
deck or an agreement, or it may have no EX-99. An 8-K whose only item is 9.01
and that has no headline files exhibits and nothing else: exhibits_only lists
them by type and the SEC's exhibit title ("EX-5.01 Opinion re legality; EX-99.01
Additional exhibits (no press release headline)"), so it holds no financial
statements despite its item's name, and is rarely worth reading for news.

Args:
    form: SEC form type (e.g. "10-K", "10-Q", "8-K", "4", "13F-HR", "S-1"), or
        several comma-separated in one call (up to 20), e.g.
        "N-CSR,N-CSRS,N-CSR/A,N-CSRS/A" or "10-K,10-K/A". Amendments are
        their own form types, so name them to include them.
    cik: Company CIK (e.g. "0000320193" or "320193")
    from_date: Start date inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD). Without cik, defaults to
        30 days before to_date (or today); pass it to reach older filings.
    to_date: End date inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)
    limit: Max results (1-100, default 100; at most 25 with include_item_text).
        For more, page with offset
    offset: Pagination offset
    item: Only 8-Ks reporting this item, by its number as the 8-K header states it,
        e.g. "5.02" (departure or election of directors or officers, officers' pay),
        "1.01" (material agreement), "2.01" (acquisition or disposal), "4.01"
        (auditor change), "5.07" (shareholder vote); several comma-separated match
        any ("1.01,2.01"). Defaults form to "8-K,8-K/A". Numbered since 2004-08-23.
        Use it instead of reading 8-Ks one by one to find, say, every director change
        this week.
    include_item_text: With item, also return each filing's text of that item
        (item_texts: item, title, text up to 10,000 characters, highlight_url marking
        it in the filing), so a screen across companies takes one call. The header
        only says 5.02; whether it is a director, a CEO or a pay plan is in the text.
    item_text: Items whose text to return with each filing, for any 10-K, 10-Q or 8-K
        (not only with item): by number or name, up to 5 comma-separated, e.g. "MD&A",
        "1A", "Risk Factors", "Part II Item 1A", "5.02". With form="10-Q" and a cik,
        "MD&A" gives a company's last several MD&As in one call. A filing without that
        Item says so in its item_texts entry ("not in this filing").
    item_text_chars: Characters of text per Item, 1,000-100,000 (default 10,000). The
        whole page carries at most 500,000 characters of text, so limit is lowered to
        fit: ask for fewer filings when you want whole MD&As.
name: get_filings
title: List Filings
